output.brief: The wrong expiry dates did not come from the agency operators or the printer firmware. The printer records show no overrides on any of the 47 Veltranol jobs. Every job from 4 Oct onward received a 36-month shelf life from the data feed, while earlier jobs, including those after the firmware change and those set up by agency operators, were correct. The cause is a Regulatory Affairs edit on 3 Oct. It entered 36 months for Veltranol with a valid-from date of March 2027, but the system fed that value to the printers anyway. Two Line 1 day-shift lots by permanent staff are affected too, and they are in the warehouse. The vendor says future-dated values cannot be sent, so that claim needs checking. The camera only compares the print with the job, so it could not catch this. Don't discipline the agency operators, and keep the camera check on. Do this next: reset the Veltranol shelf-life records, and hold and check every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the Line 1 lots. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup. Check retained cartons for HX-15-30 and MR-05-14, which also have future-dated edits. Ask Corvane to explain how a future-dated value reached the line. Other products are unconfirmed, and so is whether this began before October, though the June to 3 Oct jobs were correct. I'm fairly confident in the cause.
